note: Corpus v2, 2026-10-29: English, symbols and code only. French and Chinese are dropped; reasoning traces, science abstracts, C++ and word-problem math are added. Every other setting is copied from moe_carve_rules.json. Added 2026-10-29 before any v2 collection, for the separate slimming batch: depth (expert sizes by depth at the primary budget) and route (learned routers).

predictions.written: 2026-10-29, before any v2 collection, from the v1 result
predictions.static: Whole-stack KL above 1 nat at 0.25 again (v1: 2.50).
predictions.cluster_token: Better than both domain arms at every budget, as in v1.
predictions.domain_doc: Recovers less than half of what static loses at 0.25 (v1 ratio 0.75); math, math_word, code and code_cpp gain the most.
predictions.shared_core: At 0.25 the share of each domain set common to all domains is above v1's 0.30, because the two non-English domains are gone.
predictions.depth_shared: Within 10% of uniform cluster_token KL at 0.25: the size of the shared expert matters less than which neurons share.
predictions.depth_budget: At least 10% lower KL than uniform cluster_token at 0.25, at the same total active neurons.
predictions.route: The learned linear router's KL at 0.25 is 1.2 to 2.5 times the perfect router's; it picks 50-75% of the perfect router's experts.

criteria.primary: At budget 0.25, domain_token minus cluster_token domain-equal KL, paired document bootstrap within domains: upper 95% bound below 0 means the domain carve beats the co-activation carve; lower bound above 0 means the co-activation carve wins; otherwise a tie.
criteria.secondary: At budget 0.25, domain_doc's domain-equal KL as a fraction of static's. Under 0.5 means a document-level domain router recovers most of what a static prune loses.
criteria.tails: Copy-span mean and p99 token KL reported beside every mean; no arm is called better if its copy p99 is worse by more than 25%.
